header.label: OpenAEC Ecosystem
header.title: OpenAEC SuperCloud
header.desc: OpenAEC’s own cloud, account and SSO platform. One login for the whole ecosystem, with storage, sharing and synchronisation on your own Nextcloud server.

why.title: Why OpenAEC SuperCloud?
why.desc: Files from construction projects are often scattered across Dropbox, OneDrive and the servers of software vendors. Then someone else decides where your data lives and what it costs.
why.desc2: SuperCloud runs on your own Nextcloud. Files, accounts and issues stay on your own server, and the OpenAEC tools read and write there directly.

parts.title: Three parts
parts.desc: SuperCloud is not a single app but the layer beneath the ecosystem. These parts are being built now.
parts.p1: OpenAEC Cloud for the desktop A sync client like Dropbox: link a local folder to your Nextcloud, sync in both directions and create share links.
parts.p2: Cloud storage for the tools A shared library that lets tools such as BCF Manager Studio keep their project data in Nextcloud, with several organisations on one server.
parts.p3: One OpenAEC account One login for every app. Access tokens are checked centrally, also for AI services that work with credits.

sync.title: Two-way sync
sync.desc: Your local folder and your Nextcloud folder stay the same: new and changed files go back and forth, unchanged ones are skipped.

share.title: Share with a link
share.desc: Create a share link for a folder or file in one click, through your own server instead of an outside service.

ondemand.title: Explorer check marks
ondemand.desc: On Windows a folder becomes a cloud folder as with OneDrive: files are ready as placeholders and only download when you open them.

tenants.title: Several organisations
tenants.desc: One installation serves several organisations, each with its own projects and storage.

manifest.title: Project manifest
manifest.desc: Per project a manifest records which IFC models and issue sets belong to it, so the tools find each other’s data.

sso.title: One login
sso.desc: One account for every OpenAEC app. The desktop client now works with a Nextcloud app password; single sign-on follows.

tech.title: Technology
tech.desc: The desktop client is built with Tauri 2, Rust and SolidJS and talks to your server through WebDAV and the Nextcloud sharing API. The storage library is written in Rust, the account checks for services in Python.
